note: Part 5 SPRITES inside the demo at an arbitrary frame: 24 balls on an open ellipse (X 45 to 299 on the cosine, Y 36 to 244 on the sine, the Y phase swinging 45 degrees each way once per 256 steps so the ring leans and opens again) over eight sprites, one fixed reposition row every twenty lines, a sixteen-band gradient on $D021 rolling one band every four frames. Nothing in the window is fixed from frame to frame, so the pins are: the side borders stay the sequencer's black ($D020 is never written by the part), the window holds only the ring's colours and the balls' three (plus the 8565 grey dot, light grey, where a row writes $D021), and it is lit almost everywhere (two of the ten rows can be black: the window is 320 by 235, so at least 30,000 of 75,200 pixels are not black at any phase). PAL and NTSC are shot at different frames, so 'same' is asked only of the border. Windows in which part 5 is on screen and not yet fading: about 77M to 91M cycles PAL, 81M to 94M NTSC (the part starts about 2M later than before 2026-09-24; verify.sh's 82M and 86M are inside both).
